summary: Post-close brief for 2026-10-26; the fact layer was generated at 2026-10-26T20:37:46Z (16:37 ET), after the US cash close, so the US and A-share readings here are settled sessions rather than intraday snapshots. The composite is 62.75 and stays high_risk, regime late_cycle, down 0.43 from Friday's 63.18. The day's -2.61 is not a session-over-session move: it is measured against the 65.36 row written at 13:08 the same day, so the index drifted lower within the calendar day and was roughly flat across the weekend. Price action was a broad technical rebound: 17 of 22 sector and theme rows rose while 5 fell, mean 0.9784 and median 1.2334, with networking 3.4001, semiconductors 2.8503 and memory 1.9113 leading and fintech -3.1803 the weakest. Risk did not improve with price: macro 74.23 and liquidity_credit 74.38 together contribute 47.37%, carried by a 10-year yield at 5.0% and a Fed path pricing a December hike, while breadth stayed weak at 0.4065 above the 200-day, new lows 0.141 against new highs 0.0128. The sharpest fact of the day is divergence: the 11-name A-share memory and packaging chain fell 4.9382% on average, all 11 lower, one session after rising 3.3027% with all 11 higher.

top_risk_drivers.claim: Cross-asset confirmation stands at 0.625, the single largest contribution at 9.375 points after a 0.8 proxy discount; 5 of the 8 production signals fire: dollar strength, real-rate pressure, bitcoin down, small-cap underperformance and gold up.

HY OAS at 3.38 contributes 6.7752 points and credit spreads remain tight; but IG OAS widened from 0.89 to 0.91, so the investment-grade margin is deteriorating: not a default-cycle signal, rather a thinning valuation buffer.
VIX at 19.45, the 10-23 close, contributes 5.1048 points and is also one leg of the regime test: late_cycle requires a VIX of at least 18 and 19.45 clears it.
The 10-year real rate is 2.66 against a nominal 5.0%, mapping to a macro score of 74.23; at a 5.0% nominal level any modest rise in inflation expectations feeds straight into valuations.

The weighting itself is the risk: macro and liquidity_credit each carry 20% and together supply 29.722 of the 62.75 points, 47.37% of the composite, while volatility sits at 38.7 and trend at 45.81: the elevated reading is set by rates and credit pricing, not by price action.

supporting_signals.claim: Breadth did not repair: only 63 of 155 constituents sit above their 200-day, a 0.4065 share; index heavyweights rising masks the weakness of the median stock.
New lows at 22 against new highs at 2 on a 156-name base, a 0.141 new-low ratio versus 0.0128 for new highs: the distribution kept deteriorating alongside the broad rebound.
Small-cap weakness is structural: on a 63-session relative-strength basis IWM trails SPY by 8.8917 points, a 3-month underperformance rather than a one-day event.

The broad dollar index at 121.3202 sits above its 105 trigger and real-rate pressure at 2.66 above 1.5; the effective fed funds rate is 3.88 while FedWatch implies 4.055 for the 12-16 meeting, with the action vector pointing to a hike.

contradicting_signals.claim: Against the high_risk reading the tape was strong: networking 3.4001, semiconductors 2.8503, semiconductor equipment 2.0888, memory 1.9113, data centers 1.7175, cloud computing 1.4938 and Tesla 5.212.
The volatility dimension sits at only 38.7 and a VIX of 19.45 is not stressed; the elevated composite does not come from fear pricing.
The trend dimension is 45.81, the index sits -1.761 from its 52-week high and 5.222 above its 200-day: the price trend itself is not broken.
Credit does not confirm it: HY OAS at 3.38 and IG OAS at 0.91 both sit low and high yield has not been sold, a direct counter to the imminent-credit-event reading.

The rebound sits inside a drawdown: over the month MU is down 14.2583%, AMD down 12.5997%, AVGO down 5.8357% and NVDA down 5.6192%, so one up day has not changed the monthly direction and the bounce does not yet offset the risk reading.

what_changed_today: The composite moved from 63.18 on Friday to 62.75, a change of 0.43, still high_risk and still late_cycle.

Cross-asset confirmation fell from 0.75 to 0.625, or 6 triggers to 5; the only change was SPY turning positive at 0.7106, taking spy_down from triggered to untriggered. The cross_asset dimension fell from 75.0 to 62.5 and its contribution from 11.25 to 9.375.
The 5 US names averaged 0.6667 last session and 3.1427 today, median 2.8039; on Friday NVDA, AVGO and TSLA all fell.
The 11 A-share names reversed completely: from all 11 higher and a 3.3027 mean to all 11 lower and a 4.9382 mean, with 600584.SH down 7.8287 and 002156.SZ down 7.7815 the weakest.

The rates and FX vintages each caught up one session: the 10-year moved 5.13 to 4.96 to 5.0, VIX from 19.03 to 19.45 and the broad dollar index from 121.4048 to 121.3202; in the previous layer FX was still at 10-16.
Breadth improved marginally but stayed weak: the share above the 200-day rose from 0.3935 to 0.4065, the new-low ratio fell from 0.1603 to 0.141 and the new-high ratio fell from 0.0192 to 0.0128.
watch_next: The FOMC decision on 10-28 at 18:00Z: a hold at 3.88 is consensus, but FedWatch already implies 4.055 for the 12-16 meeting, so the real risk sits in the statement and press conference rather than in this decision.

A heavy earnings week: MSFT and GOOGL on 10-28, AMZN and INTC on 10-29, plus V and PYPL on 10-27; Microsoft offering voluntary buyouts at scale under AI capex pressure makes its cost commentary a direct input for the AI infrastructure complex.

The next A-share session in memory and packaging: it is the only opposing reading of the day, so another down day on 10-27 would point to supply-chain repricing, while a bounce would argue for a positioning event.
Whether the 10-year holds 5.0%: with the nominal rate at or above 5.0% the macro dimension at 74.23 has little room to fall, and the real rate at 2.66 is the main channel into valuations.

AI equity supply: Meta's equity-linked raise, Anthropic's IPO filing and the possible participation of Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom are the first-hand window on new supply into the AI trade, and Citadel has already flagged that the trade has almost no margin for error.

The breadth thresholds: whether the share above the 200-day keeps repairing from 0.4065 and whether the 0.141 new-low ratio rolls over; if the two keep diverging the credibility of the price rebound erodes quickly.

bull_case.title: Bull case: AI financing holds and breadth catches up to price
points: Broadcom's bank-backed AI financing, SpaceX's compute lease and Anthropic's IPO filing landed together, showing AI capex still clears the funding market; as long as financing holds, the 3.4001 networking and 2.8503 semiconductor leadership has a fundamental leg.
If the 10-year falls back below 5.0%, the macro dimension at 74.23 loosens first and the composite can move back below 60.
Breadth rising from 0.4065 and the 0.141 new-low ratio rolling over are what would turn this rebound from technical to trend.

base_case.title: Base case: high_risk chop between 60 and 65
points: The composite chops around 62.75: macro at 74.23 and liquidity_credit at 74.38 will not fall on their own, and a price rebound is unlikely to force them down.
The earnings week and the FOMC are absorbed, semis stay firm and breadth stalls near 0.4065.
The A-share and US divergence persists without becoming a cross-asset event.

bear_case.title: Bear case: a 5.0% 10-year plus December hike pricing
points: A nominal 10-year at 5.0% with a 2.66 real rate and FedWatch already at 4.055 for the 12-16 meeting: a statement that hardens the hike path leaves the 74.23 macro dimension room to rise.

The AI trade's funding dependence is the fragile point: Citadel says there is no margin for error and Musk says more than 200 neoclouds face a fight for survival, so any funding tightening reprices debt-fuelled compute expansion first.
Small caps already trail by 8.8917 points, and a 0.141 new-low ratio with 22 new lows against 2 new highs shows breadth weakening ahead of price.
